findings.title: A new packet directory permits reuse of the same delegated direction after failure
findings.scenario: The only one-start claim is packet/sequence-start.json, and the packet path is caller-selected. After a transient refused capture (not the permanently latched limits-mismatch refusal), invoke the same registration, word and still-fresh direction/host timestamps with a new packet and guard output. The old packet is never consulted; the current word remains reusable and capture allows another slot up to its three-claim bound. Thus a second sequence can reach a later successful capture and launch without the new direction required by N1.3 D12 and N1.8(aa). The attempt-directory one-use gate prevents two completed attempts, but does not prevent this forbidden retry before an attempt exists. Helper2 explicitly notes the direction-reuse limitation; it is not resolved by the packet-exclusive claim.
findings.fix: Bind a recorded direction identifier and registration digest to one durable start claim in registration-scoped state, independent of packet path, consumed before capture. A permitted restart must present a distinct newly recorded direction; retain the old claim. Add a different-packet retry case after transient capture failure; keep the limits-mismatch permanent refusal separate.
findings.evidence: Static trace at exact d2efa55014e131f92733bf2c3a90c0830214dc89. test_native_launch_sequence.py:186 tests only reuse of the identical packet after success; it cannot establish one start per direction. No sequence or reservation was executed in this review.

findings.title: Saved script and bundle pin can match disk while different sequence code is running
findings.scenario: Python loads sequence implementation A, then its source file is replaced by reviewed implementation B before main copies __file__. The retained sequence-script.py contains B, and each fresh child loads the checkout containing B. Current bundle validation hashes B at SOURCE_ROOT, and packet readback also hashes B; neither establishes that the already-loaded parent was B. A can be an older sequence lacking the reviewed stop/time behavior while the child implementation, registration and pinned on-disk B remain valid. The source-location repair avoids verifier-bootstrap imports and checks the file it names, but it does not bind executing parent code to that file. A separate orchestrator invoking the registered child checkout has the same missing association. This is a local code-replacement/startup trust gap, not a hash collision or a historical-bundle bypass.
findings.fix: Use a trusted launcher that reads and verifies the exact sequence bytes against the bundle before compiling/executing those same captured bytes, retains those exact bytes, and binds the resulting start record into the current capture/launch chain. Do not treat rereading __file__ or the mere presence of a pinned file in the child checkout as executing-code identity. Add an isolated load-A/replace-with-B witness and require refusal before capture.
findings.evidence: Static data-flow trace. test_native_launch_sequence.py:293 compares retained bytes to an unchanged file read in the test; test_native_review_bundle_v3.py:111 mutates disk and tests disk-pin refusal, not loaded-parent identity. No mutation was made to reviewed source.

findings.title: Parent input checks do not bind the bytes consumed by a child
findings.scenario: The parent remembers input bytes and checks them immediately before dispatch, but forwards mutable path names without expected digests. Replacement after _unchanged and before the child read gives the child a different internally valid registration/review/word/account-choice set. For example a second valid packet sharing the capture-state directory can cause capture under the replacement word; the parent then rejects its manifest because it is outside the original word slots, but that is after capture has occurred. A stable read inside the child detects changes during that read, not a replacement completed before it. Existing mutation tests change input during one fake step and check refusal before the next; they do not exercise the check-to-child-read window. This finding does not claim a guard for another registration can pass the existing expected guard-digest gate.
findings.fix: Pass expected input digests from the parent and have each child compare the exact bytes it will use before any effect, or dispatch from immutable captured input objects with equivalent producer/consumer binding. Add a child-start replacement regression that uses another valid input set and proves no capture is reached.
findings.evidence: Static trace of parent checks versus native_generation reads; no race or capture was run.

CHORUS.document_corpus_reason: This Dataverse record exists to publish the crate -- its four files are the crate itself, with no separate data payload. The sheet cell E16 was added on 2026-07-27 (notes/UPSTREAM_SOURCE_DISCREPANCIES.md §6), so a sheet-driven refresh would otherwise pull its landing page into data/raw/CHORUS/. Measured 2026-07-28: the page yields 14,044 characters of text against a CHORUS document bundle of ~36 KB -- a ~39% increase in the smallest corpus, which alone would confound the arm comparison. It carries the DUA link (chorus4ai.org/dataset) and the crate file names, but not the IRB protocol, institution, or confidentiality level, which appear only inside ro-crate-metadata.json. So the leak is partial, not wholesale -- and still disqualifying, because CHORUS is the GC where the crate contribution is largest and cleanest.

CM4AI.document_corpus_reason: Deliberately NOT excluded, despite being the same kind of URL as CHORUS. HIGT4C is the CM4AI data release itself; its landing page is already a curated document-corpus source (source_manifest.yaml june_2026_dataverse_release, captured 2026-07-24) and cell B16 now points at it. The crate is not on that page -- it ships inside cm4ai_release_metadata.zip, 1 of the 10 files. Excluding this DOI would silently drop a legitimate input document and change the CM4AI baseline.

AI_READI.document_corpus_reason: Not part of AI_READI's document corpus since 2026-10-14 (#5042): the owner's rule is that generation runs read no RO-Crate content, so the source_manifest.yaml entry `ro_crate_metadata` (added by #540 on 2026-08-12) was removed and the bundle rebuilt without it. The policy stays `allow` on purpose. `exclude` would register this entry's `doi` (10.60775/fairhub.3) and `describes_dataset` (fairhub.io/datasets/3) as exclusions (`rocrate_normalize.document_corpus_exclusions()`), and those name the FAIRhub dataset itself, whose records `fairhub_dataset_v3` and `fairhub_dataset_v3_api` are genuine document-corpus sources that must stay. The crate was supplied as a Drive folder, so no input-sheet citation can pull it into the corpus; leaving it out of source_manifest.yaml is what keeps it out. AI_READI records generated from 2026-08-13 to 2026-09-07 read a bundle that included it (bundle_hash_history, #5042).

VOICE.document_corpus_reason: No exclusion is possible or needed: this crate was supplied as a local directory, so it has no upstream record the sheet could cite. Its `describes_dataset` (PhysioNet b2ai-voice/3.0.0) is a genuine document corpus source in its own right and must stay -- the crate describes that release, it is not published by it.

review.details_markdown:
## Review scope and checks without findings

This is a static, adversarial review of the exact five requested commits, with d07eccefb treated as the retained draft and d2efa5501 as the final implementation. The source snapshots, diffs and both helper2 handoffs are pinned in cross-review/source-pins.json. No helper2 file was edited, no launch-sequence test was run, and no sequence-start, capture, word or attempt reservation was created. Existing tests were read as evidence of their scope, not reported as newly passing. Findings are retained locally for the lead to file; GitHub writes were forbidden.

- One invocation stops after a nonzero exit, spawn error, malformed/incomplete result, wrong manifest/guard digest or unsuccessful launch result; there is no retry loop. Same-packet concurrent/repeated starts are excluded by O_EXCL. H3-X1 concerns a different packet, not a failure of that exclusive open.
- Delegation checks both independent timestamps, rejects future times and ages above 1800 seconds, and repeats the check immediately before starting the capture command. N1 v12 bounds the sequence start, not every later guard/launch dispatch; a capture started inside the window followed by launch outside it is not itself a finding. Host confirmation, direction authenticity, starter identity and quiet-account state remain owner/lead attestations. Neither flag selects the owner-start path; supplying just one refuses.
- Child startup fixes cwd and source path, uses isolated Python and an allowlisted environment, and rejects path aliases/final symlinks at preflight. This is stronger than the retained draft. Isolated Python still trusts its interpreter/site startup; it is not a hostile-interpreter sandbox. The broader source/consumer reconstruction remains required.
- d2efa5501 trusts the physical location of native_launch_review.py: parents[2] is interpreted as the repository root, then src/data_sheets_schema/native_launch_sequence.py is read with the stable regular-file reader and hashed. A second checkout selects its own file; changed bytes refuse unless registered. In a conventional site-packages installation parents[2]/src is not the installed package path, so this read can fail closed; the sequence module has the same checkout-layout assumption. The production runbook requires the registered source checkout, so I do not grade unsupported wheel execution as a defect. This disk-source check does not solve H3-X2.
- Current native_generation capture/guard/record-word, capture current authority, subscription preflight/context, execution authorizations and admit all require current review. Bundle v2/terms v1 remain accepted only in historical readers; no current launch bypass through that pair was found. Mixed versions refuse, integer 1 is not accepted as account_quiet, and current terms explicitly require the value to be True. The sequence pin must equal the registration package-source pin and current source bytes. Packet readback hashes the retained bytes independently, not a sequence.json claim.
- Latest capture is enforced in current_guard_preparation under words.locked, including _read_capture_records_at_root(require_latest=True) and _checked_claim_selection; execution repeats _require_latest_guard_claim under the same word lock held through attempt.mkdir. Both the accepted shared-selection branch and the other execution branch do so. Historical readback deliberately does not require today's latest claim. The sequence test named test_latest_capture_refusal_is_terminal only simulates a nonzero guard command; it proves stop propagation, not latest-claim semantics. The separate test_native_latest_capture_claim.py carries those mutation/locking checks. No new false-positive assertion was identified in that migration; the concrete coverage gaps are attached to H3-X1 to X3.
- N1.8(ab)'s reservation-to-dispatch measurement and the proposed margin remain separate engineering/owner prerequisites. This read-only review did not exercise or settle them.

## Part A findings and interpretation

H3-A1 (P2, fixed locally): scripts/build_native_canary_packet.py originally rejected every project except CHORUS at lines 98-99. CM4AI's first saved builder outcome is exactly "this reviewed packet prefix is scoped to CHORUS". Commit 0cf319823 replaces the hardcoded gate with the existing manifest-declared project/bundle check. No production validator, data, prompt or protected file changed. The fixed CM4AI canary passed alone before the other four prefix executions. This is a Part A builder finding, excluded from the helper2 review counts.

The initial test launcher refused the restored composition status before running tests; its hash/HEAD checks are retained and it now accepts that explicit restored state. The first test attempt then failed because the harness passed a relative registry bundle to the absolute-path builder. That failed cohort is retained; the harness now resolves the path and saves child errors. The subsequent original-builder canary records the actual project restriction. A recording test passing means its evidence assertions passed; prefix acceptance is taken only from status.json dependency_stop and nonempty receipt/selection/inventory artifacts.

All five baseline document bundles and chunk manifests are current. Explicit absolute --manifest audit invocations report staleness because concatenate_documents.py:213 writes that string into the header. The default repository invocation uses the recorded relative manifest string; all five rebuilt baseline files have empty diffs and matching hashes. Thus the first results do not establish content drift. Commands were launched from the explicit physical composition cwd; using its canonical relative manifest spelling for this comparison is deliberate. No repository corpus was regenerated or overwritten. Historical nonbaseline audit gaps remain visible: CM4AI with-crate lacks ai_ready_score.json, and crate-only/healthsheet-only arms have no rebuild route.
